spec.description: Scrape failures plus sparse InnerTube player() responses that can create unusable video-min files. Sparse player responses are grouped by bounded reason_class/status so content restrictions can be separated from client/proxy soft blocks.
spec.title: Scrape failures and sparse player responses

spec.description: Channel-to-channel discovery outcomes per scraped channel. Existing links: already_scraped (creator_map) + on_exchange (scrape.exchange already has it). New links: enqueued with source=discovered_link. Skipped links: self_link, below_min_subscribers, resolve_failed, exchange_check_failed.
spec.title: Channel link discovery: existing vs new links /s

spec.description: Rate (5m) of subscriber count parse attempts on scraped YouTube channel pages, split by outcome: found, absent (the page shows no count), and unparseable (count text present but not parseable). is_retry=true marks a forced missing-subscriber retry scrape.
spec.title: Subscriber count parses /s by scraper / source / outcome

spec.description: Rate (5m) at which the rate limiter picks each proxy (power of two choices over healthy proxies). With even spreading every proxy carries a similar share; a proxy near zero is in cooldown or failing.
spec.title: Proxy selections /s by proxy

spec.description: Fleet-wide exponentially weighted transport failure rate (connection, tunnel, pool, TLS errors) per proxy, as last seen by each process. Above 0.5 a failure puts the proxy in cooldown. Values a process has not updated in 30 min are hidden: processes only refresh proxies they select, so idle scrapers keep stale readings.
spec.title: Proxy transport failure rate (EWMA) by proxy

spec.description: Proxies currently skipped by proxy selection after transport failures (30 s cooldown, doubling per reopening up to 10 min). "total" is the number of proxies in cooldown. Readings a process has not updated in 30 min are hidden as stale.
spec.title: Proxies in cooldown

spec.description: Number of times each proxy was put in cooldown over the last hour. A proxy that keeps reopening has a broken tunnel or exit node.
spec.title: Proxy cooldowns (1h) by proxy

spec.description: InnerTube search result pages requested by yt_discover_search.py (5m rate), by outcome and page type. failed = no page after retries.
spec.title: Search pages /s by outcome

spec.description: Failed search request attempts by exception type (5m rate). Transport errors point at proxies; InnerTube request/response errors at YouTube.
spec.title: Search errors /s by type

spec.description: Duration of one InnerTube search call, excluding the rate-limiter wait.
spec.title: Search latency p50/p95

spec.description: Channels extracted from search pages by facet (before dedupe), next to what happened when they were offered to the channel scrape queue: enqueued (new), already_scraped / on_exchange (known), below_min_subscribers, ...
spec.title: Discovery yield: channels found vs enqueue outcome /s

spec.description: Channels newly enqueued per successful search page (1h). The best single measure of whether discovery earns its search budget; expect it to fall as markets get exhausted.
spec.title: New channels enqueued per search page

spec.description: Fraction of search pages that failed after retries, per market (gl), over 1h; the 10 worst markets.
spec.title: Search page failure ratio by market (top 10)

spec.description: Market x term x facet search jobs completed per hour, and the jobs planned in the current round.
spec.title: Discovery jobs completed /h

spec.description: Over the last 24h: channels (search) are new channels yt_discover_search added to the channel scrape queue; videos (RSS) are video IDs the RSS scraper found that the video queue had never seen (not already queued, scraped or uploaded).
spec.title: Discovered (24h)

spec.description: Current queue size divided by the assets scraped in the last day, in days.
spec.title: Days to process the video queue

spec.description: Active (scheduled) channels by how completely their video IDs have been listed: complete = every tab paged to the end; partial = scraped but not yet fully listed; pre_tracking = last scraped before progress tracking; never_scraped = no scrape yet.
spec.title: Channel video listing status (stacked)

spec.expr:
sum by (tier) (max by (tier, status) (channel_video_listing_status{status="complete",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))
/
sum by (tier) (max by (tier, status) (channel_video_listing_status{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))

spec.description: Share of active channels in each tier whose video IDs have been listed completely.
spec.title: Channel video listing: % complete per tier

spec.description: One-time full listings of a channel's videos, shorts and live tabs: completed marks the channel complete; incomplete means paging stopped early and is retried on the next scrape.
spec.title: Channel full listings (1h) by outcome

spec.description: Known IDs per state; leased = popped and not yet completed or marked.
spec.title: Backlog items by state

spec.description: IDs handed to scrapers and not yet resolved.
spec.title: Backlog leased IDs

spec.description: Expired leases are re-queued at the back of the priority lane. Sustained non-zero means scrapers die or hold IDs longer than BACKLOG_LEASE_SECS.
spec.title: Backlog leases expired

spec.description: scrape_duration_seconds: time of one scrape, not counting time spent waiting for rate-limiter tokens or in retry/penalty backoff. The waits are in scrape_wait_seconds.
spec.title: YouTube scrape duration p50/p95/p99 by entity (excl. rate-limit wait)

spec.description: In-memory changes not yet merged into the base generation.
spec.title: Backlog delta entries

spec.description: Malformed video IDs rejected by the server.
spec.title: Backlog invalid IDs

spec.description: Upload-state lookups the backlog server could not answer and scrape-upload asked the scrape.exchange API about, while BACKLOG_UPLOADED_API_FALLBACK=true (the uploaded-state migration). Empty when the fallback is off.
spec.title: Upload-state API fallback lookups

spec.description: InnerTube get_panel requests that fetch the transcript of a video (youtube_transcript_scrapes_total). Outcomes: success; unavailable (no_panel: YouTube offers no transcript for the video, e.g. live streams or no captions; empty: the panel had no segments); failure (rate_limited: HTTP 429, rate_wait: no rate-limit token within the wait cap, http_error, transport, timeout, parse_error, other). Failures never fail the video scrape. rate_limited and rate_wait rising mean TRANSCRIPT_REFILL_PER_MIN is too high for YouTube or the proxies.
spec.title: Video transcript fetches /s by outcome and reason

spec.description: Time of one successful video scrape attempt, not counting rate-limiter token waits or retry/penalty backoff (scrape_duration_seconds, scraper=video_scraper): InnerTube calls, channel enrichment and the file write. Split by innertube_calls, the YouTube calls the attempt sent: player, next, transcript (get_panel), ytdlp, channel_browse (handle lookup missed the creator map). Compare player_next with player_next_transcript to see what the transcript fetch costs.
spec.title: Video scrape attempt duration p50/p95 by InnerTube calls

spec.description: Number of yt-dlp extract_info calls currently in the thread pool. Pins near executor ceiling (≈12 per process) when GIL / executor is the bottleneck.
spec.title: yt-dlp extract_info active (thread-pool occupancy)

spec.description: api_request_duration_seconds: one HTTP request to YouTube, timed after the rate-limiter token was granted. call is html, player, next, get_panel (transcript), browse (channel tabs) or resolve_url (handle to channel ID).
spec.title: YouTube API request p50/p95 by call

spec.description: Bytes received per second of body transfer: sum of response bytes (as received, before decompression) divided by the sum of body time (headers to last byte), over InnerTube and HTML calls. A bandwidth-capped proxy shows here even when its connections are reused.
spec.title: Response throughput by proxy_file

spec.description: Body throughput per API call (player, next, get_panel, browse, resolve_url, html). Small responses are dominated by round-trip time, so their throughput reads lower than large ones on the same path.
spec.title: Response throughput by call

spec.description: Time from sending the request to receiving the response headers: YouTube's processing time plus one round trip through the proxy.
spec.title: Response wait (request sent → headers) p50/p95 by proxy_file

spec.description: Time to receive the response body after the headers arrived. Grows with response size and with limited proxy bandwidth.
spec.title: Response body time (headers → last byte) p50/p95 by proxy_file

spec.description: Response body size as received over the network (compressed).
spec.title: Response size p50/p95 by call

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50 , sum by (le, method, status_class, instance) (rate(exchange_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[10m])))

spec.title: scrape.exchange API request p50/p95 by method × status_class
RSS tier SLA — on-time vs overdue rate
RSS: seconds since channel last processed

spec.description: Live queue depth per entity. RSS uses scrape_queue_size (set once at scraper startup; reflects the seed working set). Channel uses channel_queue_tier_size summed across tiers. Video uses video_state_size{state="queued"} (Redis-backed; max-by-state collapses the duplicate per-host publishers).
spec.title: Total queue depth

spec.description: Per-proxy_file success and failure rate (5m) of RSS feed fetches by the RSS scraper. Use this to spot networks where the RSS path is degrading. Compare with the YouTube scraper's circuit-breaker panel to see whether degradation tripped the limiter.
spec.title: RSS fetch Failure rate

spec.description: Per-proxy_file success and failure rate (5m) of InnerTube channel.info calls made by the RSS scraper. Use to spot networks where InnerTube channel resolution is degrading.
spec.title: InnerTube Channel fail rate by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the TCP handshake to the proxy on RSS fetches. Histograms only record fresh connection establishment — keep-alive reuse skips the trace event, so _count reflects new tunnels, not total fetches.
spec.title: RSS TCP connect duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the HTTP CONNECT exchange (proxy dialing YouTube on our behalf) on RSS fetches. The gap between connect_tcp.complete and start_tls.started — i.e. the proxy backend's dial-out queue.
spec.title: RSS HTTP CONNECT tunnel duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the TLS handshake to YouTube via the proxy tunnel on RSS fetches. Slowness here — with fast TCP and HTTP CONNECT — indicates YouTube is throttling TLS from the proxy's egress IP rather than provider-side queueing.
spec.title: RSS TLS handshake duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the TCP handshake to the proxy on YouTube HTML fetches (channel about-page, home, search, session warm-up). Sourced from curl's CURLINFO_CONNECT_TIME minus CURLINFO_NAMELOOKUP_TIME. Histograms only record fresh connection establishment — keep-alive reuse skips because curl reports 0 for the connect-related fields on reuse.
spec.title: HTML TCP connect duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the TLS handshake (plus HTTP CONNECT tunnel exchange for proxied requests) on YouTube HTML fetches. Sourced from curl's CURLINFO_APPCONNECT_TIME minus CURLINFO_CONNECT_TIME. Note: curl reports app-connect cumulatively, so the HTTP CONNECT exchange cannot be split out separately as it is on RSS — both are bundled here. Slowness with fast TCP indicates YouTube is throttling TLS from the proxy's egress IP or the provider's CONNECT-tunnel queue is backed up.
spec.title: HTML TLS handshake (+CONNECT) duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the TCP handshake to the proxy on InnerTube calls (channel.browse / video.player). Sourced from httpcore trace events on the third-party innertube library's httpx.Client session. Histograms only record fresh connection establishment — keep-alive reuse skips the trace event.
spec.title: InnerTube TCP connect duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the HTTP CONNECT exchange (proxy dialing YouTube on our behalf) on InnerTube calls. Gap between connect_tcp.complete and start_tls.started — the proxy backend's dial-out queue.
spec.title: InnerTube HTTP CONNECT tunnel duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: p50 / p95 of the TLS handshake to YouTube via the proxy tunnel on InnerTube calls. Slowness with fast TCP + fast CONNECT indicates YouTube is throttling TLS from the proxy's egress IP.
spec.title: InnerTube TLS handshake duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

spec.description: Fraction of requests that reused an existing pooled TCP connection (didn't need a new TCP+CONNECT+TLS handshake). High = the TLS handshake cost amortises across many requests; low = every fetch pays the full handshake cost, and the TLS p95 numbers turn into your wall-clock floor. Broken out by call_type so you can see whether RSS/InnerTube/HTML pools are reusing equally well.
spec.title: Keep-alive reuse rate by call_type

spec.expr: sum by (call_type, proxy_file) (rate(proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) / clamp_max(sum by (call_type, proxy_file) (rate(proxy_requests_total{reused="false",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[5m])), 100)

spec.description: Average requests per fresh TCP connection. A value of 1 means every request opens a fresh connection (worst case — full handshake cost per fetch). 10 means each connection serves 10 requests on average before the pool retires it. Higher is better; large differences across proxy_files indicate that some providers terminate the keep-alive earlier than others.
spec.title: Requests per fresh connection by call_type x proxy_file

spec.description: Number of channels currently in each workflow state. Gauges are published by one elected worker per host, so max-by-state collapses the duplicate series.
spec.title: Channel queue: state size (stacked)

spec.description: Channels scheduled per tier (parallel to RSS tier population).
spec.title: Channel queue: tier population

spec.description: Resolve-phase outcomes per attempt. Outcomes: promoted (success), not_found, inconsistent_identity, backoff (transient retry), unresolved (gave up).
spec.title: Channel queue: resolve outcomes /s

spec.description: Scrape-phase outcomes per attempt. Outcomes: scraped (success), not_found, terminated, soft_unavailable (transient), unresolved (no handle in creator_map).
spec.title: Channel queue: scrape outcomes /s

spec.description: Number of videos currently in each workflow state. Gauge is published by one elected worker per host, so max-by-state collapses the duplicate series.
spec.title: Video queue: state size (stacked)

spec.description: Per-attempt outcomes in the video scrape queue. Outcomes: scraped (success or already-uploaded dedup), retried (transient failure, bump_attempts), unavailable (private / age-gated / removed), failed (other or transient retries exhausted).
spec.title: Video queue: outcomes /s

spec.description: Duration of each non-home channel tab scrape. Split by tab and outcome to identify slow videos/shorts/live/post/store work inside full channel scrapes. Excludes time spent waiting for rate-limiter tokens or in backoff sleeps.
spec.title: Channel tab scrape duration p50/p95

spec.description: Rate of InnerTube tab pages fetched by initial vs continuation page. Continuation-heavy tabs are the likely source of slow channel work.
spec.title: Channel tab pages fetched /s

spec.description: Rate of parsed IDs and objects from channel tabs. Compare against page fetch rate to spot tabs that burn requests without yielding much useful content.
spec.title: Channel tab items parsed /s

spec.description: Full channel scrape attempts completed in each hour: success, failure, terminal or superseded. A full scrape runs on every tenth successful channel refresh per the per-channel cadence stored in the queue.
spec.title: Channel full scrapes (1h) by outcome

spec.description: Histogram of video IDs added to the scrape queue per full channel scrape attempt, including zero. Wide spikes mean a large channel was successfully enumerated.
spec.title: Channel full scrape: IDs added per attempt (p50/p95)

spec.description: Video IDs processed by full channel scrapes per second, labelled found, existing, added, queue_known or failed. A climbing failed rate while added stays flat means queue or exchange delivery problems.
spec.title: Channel full scrape: video IDs /s by outcome
